elements.element: Vendor has an express duty to defend Customer and its affiliates.
elements.evidence: Retained Section 14.1: "RevMed shall indemnify, defend and hold harmless Sanofi, its Affiliates and their respective officers, directors, agents and employees ('Sanofi Indemnitees')" — express defence duty running to Customer and its Affiliates.

elements.element: Vendor indemnifies Customer and its affiliates against third-party claims.
elements.evidence: Section 14.1 lead-in covers "any Third Party Claims and Losses arising therefrom under or related to this Agreement" in favour of the Sanofi Indemnitees (Sanofi and its Affiliates); "Third Party Claims" is a defined term (1.126).

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers claims that Services or Deliverables infringe intellectual property rights.
elements.evidence: New limb (d): "any Third Party Claim alleging that the RevMed Licensed Technology, or Sanofi's exercise of the licenses granted to it under this Agreement, infringes or misappropriates the intellectual property rights of a Third Party." There are no "Services" or "Deliverables" in this collaboration/licence structure; "RevMed Licensed Technology" (defined at 1.99) plus exercise of the granted licences is the correct analogue, so the element is met in substance. The deterministic check "vendor indemnity for IP infringement present: false" keys on the absent Services/Deliverables vocabulary (and reflects the pre-redline baseline); inspected substantively, the operative limb supplies the IP indemnity.

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers Vendor's breach of applicable law.
elements.evidence: New limb (f): "RevMed's breach of Applicable Law" — a free-standing limb that does not depend on the double-materiality filter in retained limb (c)/Section 13.4(b); "Applicable Law" is defined at 1.8.

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers a data breach caused by Vendor.
elements.evidence: New limb (e): "any unauthorized access to, or disclosure of, Sanofi's Confidential Information or other Sanofi data caused by RevMed" — causation by Vendor is express.

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers Vendor's gross negligence and wilful misconduct.
elements.evidence: Retained limb (a): "the negligence, recklessness or willful misconduct of any of the RevMed Indemnitees" — ordinary negligence subsumes gross negligence, and wilful misconduct is named.

elements.element: The indemnification procedure requires notice of a claim.
elements.evidence: Section 14.3(a): "The Indemnified Party will give the indemnifying Party ... prompt written notice (an 'Indemnification Claim Notice') of any Losses ..." and the notice applies to claims "under Section 14.1 or Section 14.2", so it picks up the new limbs automatically.

elements.element: The indemnification procedure allocates control of the defence.
elements.evidence: Section 14.3(b) Control of Defense: "At its option, the Indemnifying Party may assume the defense of any Third Party Claim subject to indemnification as provided for in Section 14.1 or Section 14.2 ... may select and appoint the lead legal counsel."

elements.element: The indemnification procedure requires reasonable cooperation.
elements.evidence: Section 14.3(e) Cooperation: "the Indemnified Party will, and will cause each other Indemnitee to, cooperate in the defense thereof and will furnish such records, information and testimony ... as may be reasonably requested."

elements.element: Customer indemnity is limited to Customer-provided content and Customer's breach of law.
elements.evidence: Section 14.2 as rendered contains only "(a) any content, data or materials provided by Sanofi to RevMed under this Agreement; or (b) Sanofi's breach of Applicable Law", with former limbs (c) and (d) marked "[Intentionally omitted.]" and the former Research/Development/Manufacture/Commercialization and Sanofi-negligence limbs removed.

elements.element: Vendor indemnifies Customer against third-party intellectual-property claims.
elements.evidence: New Section 14.1(d) covers Third Party Claims that the RevMed Licensed Technology or Sanofi's exercise of the granted licences infringes or misappropriates Third Party IP rights.

elements.element: The IP indemnity may exclude infringement caused by Customer modifications.
elements.evidence: Permissive element: no modification carve-out is included, which is Customer-favourable and therefore does not defeat the element ("may exclude").

elements.element: The IP indemnity may exclude infringement caused by Customer combinations.
elements.evidence: Permissive element: no combination carve-out is included; the absence of a permitted exclusion is favourable to Customer and does not fail the checklist.

elements.element: The IP indemnity may exclude infringement caused by Customer specifications.
elements.evidence: Permissive element: no specification carve-out is included; again favourable to Customer, so the condition does not apply.

elements.element: Vendor must procure continued use, modify, or replace the infringing item.
elements.evidence: Nothing in the rendered Article XIV (or Article XIII) obliges RevMed to procure continued rights, modify or replace infringing technology; Section 10.7 only requires the Parties to negotiate a Third Party licence.

elements.element: Vendor must refund applicable fees if procure, modify, or replace remedies are unavailable.
elements.evidence: No refund-of-fees remedy appears anywhere in the rendered language; there is no fall-back monetary remedy tied to failure of the (absent) procure/modify/replace ladder.

elements.element: Vendor's indemnity is subject to a super-cap of three times annual fees.
elements.evidence: No 3x annual-fees super-cap is inserted; the drafter expressly declined it, and "annual fees" has no analogue in this upfront/milestone/royalty structure.

reasons: Position-complete at the preferred level: all ten preferred elements are met in operative language. Limbs (d)-(f) supply the missing IP-infringement, data-breach and breach-of-Applicable-Law heads; limbs (a) and the Section 14.3 machinery were already compliant and were correctly left untouched.

The deterministic flag "vendor indemnity for IP infringement present: false" is a vocabulary artefact (the agreement has no "Services"/"Deliverables"); inspected in substance, new Section 14.1(d) is a genuine, unqualified IP infringement/misappropriation indemnity keyed to the defined term "RevMed Licensed Technology" (Section 1.99) and to Sanofi's exercise of the granted licences.

Fallback is incomplete (no procure/modify/replace ladder, no refund remedy, no 3x super-cap), but that is immaterial because the preferred level is complete; the drafter's reasons for declining the super-cap (it would cap a presently uncapped indemnity under Section 14.5) are sound and consistent with not flagging Customer-favourable terms.

Minimal: the edits are confined to the checklist. The conforming change of the exception lead-in from "(a) through (c)" to "(a) through (f)" is necessary to avoid a dangling cross-reference; the deletions in Section 14.2 are required by the tenth preferred element; no survival tail, expense allocation, extra damages categories or boilerplate was added. Limb (e)'s reference to "Sanofi's Confidential Information or other Sanofi data" is an acceptable proxy for an undefined "Customer Data" and covers all data belonging to or supplied by Customer rather than selected categories.

Preserves intent: the Section 14.1 carve-outs (i)-(iii) for Sanofi negligence and Sanofi breach survive without contradiction and now properly reach the new limbs; Section 14.3's notice/control/cooperation machinery references "Section 14.1 or Section 14.2" generically and needs no amendment; no defined term is left undefined and the "[Intentionally omitted.]" placeholders preserve internal lettering.

Drafting nit (not a failure): limb (d) reads "arising or resulting from ... any Third Party Claim alleging that ..." against a lead-in that already covers "Third Party Claims". Consider trimming (d) to "an allegation that the RevMed Licensed Technology, or Sanofi's exercise of the licenses granted to it under this Agreement, infringes or misappropriates the intellectual property rights of a Third Party" to remove the circularity.

Practical check before sending: confirm that no other provision (e.g., insurance, the Profit/Loss Share Agreement, or product-liability cost-sharing) cross-refers to the deleted Section 14.2(a)-(d) limbs, since removing Sanofi's Commercialization and negligence indemnities is a substantial reallocation that RevMed will resist; the narrowing is checklist-required, but a residual product-liability cost-share reference would need conforming.
